items.claim: A+B nonzero fill whose outlines meet only at vertices or along a shared stretch skips crossing resolution (A; B's crossing-related findings are separate)
nestRings box test runs before the tolerant on-outline check, so a ring on its container's edge stays top-level

A cut between two anchors, or between an anchor and a curve's first interior point, snaps to the nearer anchor's color in trim, dash, clip windows and fill crossings, with the rule copied in `anchorsAlong`
Nonzero crossing resolution has no work cap, unlike even-odd
items.note: question (should it have one? The even-odd cap falls back to the parity stencil, and the renderer has no nonzero stencil, so a cap could only draw a wrong fill instead of a slow one; a real cap needs a nonzero stencil pass in the renderer. I left it uncapped and recorded the call in `docs/unruled.md`.)

items.claim: resolveCrossings ignores an incomplete chain, so a nonzero fill loses a face
items.note: + c2fcd2d5fd. A fuzz found this on ordinary integer polygons, not only after `weld`. Root cause: `boundaryPieces` judged each side of a piece by the winding at a point offset 1e-7 of the outline's size, and a hairline spike or a near-triple crossing is narrower than that, so the piece was misjudged. It now counts the winding on a ray from the piece's midpoint (f192eb03c6), and 100,000 fuzz trials under both rules all close. c2fcd2d5fd also makes the nonzero path fall back to the unresolved outline when a boundary still won't close, as even-odd falls back to the stencil; that call is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.
